identity.name: Portuguese Africa
alt_names: African possessions of the Portuguese Empire

land.text: the Moroccan, Gold Coast, Cape Verde and Sao Tome patches of the Portuguese Empire's 1502-1506 shape, which Cliopatria moves to its own Portuguese Africa row in 1507

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Portuguese Empire row (1502-1823) draws these patches until 1506 and the Portuguese Africa row from 1507; the Sofala, Mozambique Island, Zanzibar-Pemba-Mafia and Socotra patches are new in the Portuguese Africa row. The change of row is Cliopatria's convention: no page opened dates a 1507 event.

land.text: all 99 cells of the 1579 shape reappear in Cliopatria's Spanish Empire row from 1582

successors.note: Cliopatria's Iberian Union row (1582-1639) holds none of these cells; its Spanish Empire row does. The pages opened say the opposite of a change of ruler: at Tomar in 1581 Philip II was crowned Philip I of Portugal and promised to keep the empires legally distinct, and the Evolution page has Tangier Portuguese to 1662, Mazagan to 1769, Elmina to 1637 and Cape Verde, Mozambique and Angola continuing as Portuguese colonies. The hand-over is Cliopatria's drawing, not a historical transfer.

capitals.name: Lisbon
capitals.note: The Portuguese Empire page's infobox lists Lisbon as the capital and no other. The row has no African seat of government: the Mozambique page gives Cidade de Pedra (Island of Mozambique) as capital of the Mozambique territory from 1507, and the Evolution page has Mozambique subordinate to Goa 1501-1569. Shown at Lisbon because the holdings were governed from there.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1507 shape unchanged for 1507-1510 (Safi to Mazagan, Tangier, Ceuta and Ksar es-Seghir, Cape Verde, Sao Tome, Fernando Po, the Gold Coast around Elmina, Sofala, Mozambique Island, the Zanzibar-Pemba-Mafia coast, Socotra), plus Arguin

keyframe_review.note: 34,831 km2 of scattered enclaves; the shape stands for 1507-1510 and is cut short because Socotra, 'possession (1506-1511)', leaves in 1511 (see portuguese-africa_1511). Pages: Safi '1488-1541', Mazagan '1506-1769', Alcacer Ceguer '1458-1550', Arzila '1471-1550', Tangier '1471-1662', Elmina '1482-1637', Cape Verde 'settlements (1462-1495)'; the Mozambique page has the territory established in 1505 and Cidade de Pedra the capital from 1507. Arguin ('1455-1633') is added because the page lists it and the shape lacks it (the Portuguese Empire page puts the first Arguin feitoria in 1445). Not dated by any page opened: Sao Tome, Fernando Po and the Zanzibar-Pemba-Mafia cells (unverified: page budget). No infobox area exists (the Portuguese Africa article is a maintenance stub), so no ratio.

correction.text: the 1507 shape without Socotra ('possession (1506-1511)'), plus Arguin

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria keeps the 18 Socotra cells (Yemen) in this row until 1533, but the Evolution page gives 'Socotra: possession (1506-1511)'; the Portuguese Empire page has the fleet conquering Socotra in 1506. Everything else in the shape stands for 1511-1533.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1534 shape unchanged for 1534-1540 (the 1507 shape without Socotra, plus Inhambane, the Zambezi-delta coast and two more Gold Coast cells), plus Arguin

The Mozambique page dates only the 1530s trading posts and garrisons at Sena and Tete on the Zambezi, which are not in the shape, and Maputo Bay explored in 1544; the Inhambane and delta cells are unverified: page budget. region.text: Cliopatria's 1507 shape (Moroccan enclaves, Cape Verde, Sao Tome, Fernando Po, the Gold Coast at Elmina, Sofala, Mozambique Island, the Zanzibar-Pemba-Mafia coast, Socotra) plus Arguin ('1455-1633')

ledger.note: 1507: the African possessions of the Portuguese Empire become a row of their own. The date is Cliopatria's (its first Portuguese Africa shape, 34,831 km2); the Mozambique page gives the territory 'established' in 1505 and Cidade de Pedra as capital from 1507, the Evolution page the Portuguese presence in Africa from 1415 with Ceuta. Page silent on any 1507 event.

1511: Socotra leaves Portuguese hands. Evolution row 'Socotra: possession (1506-1511)'; the Portuguese Empire page has the fleet conquering it in 1506. Neither page says who ended the possession; the Evolution row continues 'Became part of Mahri', so the counterpart is the Mahra Sultanate (no dossier yet; reviewer af-08-a).

region.text: the cells the 1534 shape adds to the 1507 shape: the coast at Inhambane and on the Zambezi delta, and two more on the Gold Coast

ledger.note: 1534: Cliopatria's shape adds twelve cells (Inhambane, the Zambezi-delta coast, two on the Gold Coast). The Mozambique page dates only the 1530s garrisons and trading posts at Sena and Tete on the Zambezi and Maputo Bay explored in 1544; page silent on the cells themselves.

region.text: the Safi-Azemmour strip of Atlantic Morocco, 'Safim/Safi 1488-1541' and 'Azamor/Azemmour 1513-1541'

ledger.note: 1541: the Portuguese give up Safi and Azemmour (and lose Agadir) to the Saadis. the page has the Portuguese abandoning Safi in 1541 after Saadi offensives and Azemmour in 1541 too, and Agadir was captured by the Saadis in 1541 under Mohammed ash-Sheikh. Cliopatria keeps the strip to 1546.

region.text: Ksar es-Seghir (Alcacer Ceguer) and Asilah (Arzila) on the Strait coast of Morocco

ledger.note: 1550: Alcacer-Ceguer (Ksar es-Seghir) and Arzila (Asilah) are abandoned. Evolution rows 'Alcacer Ceguer/El Qsar es Seghir - colony - 1458-1550' and 'Arzila/Asilah - colony - 1471-1550; 1577-1589'; the conflicts page has Alcacer abandoned in 1549 and Arzila in 1550. Tangier stays Portuguese.

region.text: six cells on the Guinea coast around Cacheu (Cliopatria's 1564 addition)

ledger.note: 1564: Cliopatria's shape adds six cells on the Cacheu coast of Guinea. No page opened dates a Portuguese holding there; the Cape Verde page has only the 1466 trading rights across West Africa except Arguim, which the king rescinded a few years later.

region.text: Luanda, established by Paulo Dias de Novais in 1576

ledger.note: 1576: Paulo Dias de Novais founds Luanda. the page has Paulo Dias de Novais establishing Luanda in 1576, soon a slave port; the Evolution page has Angola a colony from 1575. The page names no previous holder; the portuguese-angola dossier also enters the founding against nobody.
1577: Arzila (Asilah) is Portuguese again. Evolution row 'Arzila/Asilah - colony - 1471-1550; 1577-1589'. The page does not say from whom.

region.text: the last Cliopatria shape of Portuguese Africa, all of it carried into the Spanish Empire row in 1582

ledger.note: 1581: the Cortes of Tomar crown Philip II of Spain as Philip I of Portugal, who promised, the page says, to keep the empires legally distinct. Cliopatria closes the Portuguese Africa row here and draws the same 99 cells in its Spanish Empire row from 1582; the Evolution page shows the holdings continuing as Portuguese (Tangier to 1662, Mazagan to 1769, Elmina to 1637, Cape Verde a crown colony from 1587, Angola a crown colony from 1589).

wars.name: Moroccan-Portuguese conflicts

zones.text: Safi, Azemmour and Agadir, abandoned or lost in 1541
Alcacer-Ceguer and Arzila, abandoned in 1550; Arzila retaken in 1577

wars.outcome: The Portuguese hold the Atlantic enclaves until the Saadi offensives of 1541 take Agadir and force the abandonment of Safi and Azemmour; Alcacer-Ceguer and Arzila follow in 1549-1550. Tangier and Mazagan stay Portuguese; Arzila is held again 1577-1589.
wars.note: The page's umbrella article runs 1415-1769. The Moroccan enclaves have their own dossier (portuguese-morocco) with page-dated events from 1415; this entry lists only what the Cliopatria row's cells needed.

wars.name: Battle of Alcácer Quibir
wars.outcome: 4 August 1578 at Ksar-el-Kebir: Moroccan forces destroy the Portuguese army and King Sebastian is killed; the defeat leads to the succession crisis of 1580 and the union with Spain. No enclave changes hands.
wars.note: Listed because it opens the road to the Iberian Union that ends this row in Cliopatria; no territorial result in Africa.

wars.name: Ndongo warfare after the Kabasa massacre
wars.outcome: In 1579 the Ndongo ruler massacred Portuguese and Kongolese residents at Kabasa; warfare with Ndongo continued for decades. No land changes hands within this row's life.
wars.note: The Portuguese Empire page gives no battle names for these years; the title is descriptive. The later conquest belongs to the portuguese-angola and kingdom-of-ndongo dossiers.

certainty.note: Every holding is a fort or town enclave (the Moroccan coast, Elmina, Cape Verde, Mozambique Island, Sofala, Luanda) whose hinterland no page defines; the Mozambique captaincy had no surveyed extent and the Moroccan enclave limits are the cities' immediate ground. No boundary in the row rests on a treaty line or survey.

notes:
PORTUGUESE AFRICA (Cliopatria row 1507-1581, 5 shapes). Page budget used: six pages including the empty state article.

NO ARTICLE. Wikipedia 'Portuguese Africa' is a maintenance stub (no infobox, no dates), so there is no infobox area to compare with Cliopatria's 28,900-35,685 km2; the Portuguese Mozambique page gives an area only for the early 1970s. The title Portuguese_Morocco does not exist on Wikipedia (URL not found, tried once). The state is built from the Portuguese Empire, Evolution of the Portuguese Empire, Moroccan-Portuguese conflicts, Portuguese Mozambique and History of Cape Verde pages.

THE ROW IS A COMPOSITE THAT OTHER DOSSIERS ALSO CARRY. Cliopatria's Portuguese Africa shape is a set of enclaves: Safi to Mazagan and the Tangier-Ceuta strip (Morocco), Cape Verde, Sao Tome, Fernando Po and the Elmina coast (Gulf of Guinea), Sofala and Mozambique Island, the Zanzibar-Pemba-Mafia coast, Socotra, from 1564 six cells in Guinea and from 1579 Luanda. Dossiers written by other groups cover the same land under their own slugs: portuguese-morocco (1415-1769, Moroccan enclaves, its notes already say the integrator must choose), portuguese-mozambique (1505-1975), portuguese-angola (1575-1975), portuguese-empire (1415-1910, which by its own note leaves the African patches to this row from 1507), kilwa-sultanate (occupation 1505-1513). For 1507-1581 the integrator should draw each cell once. Recommended: use portuguese-morocco, portuguese-mozambique and portuguese-angola for their land (they carry more events), and use this dossier for what no colony dossier holds: Cape Verde, Sao Tome, Fernando Po, the Gold Coast at Elmina, Guinea (from 1564), Socotra (to 1510) and the Zanzibar-Pemba-Mafia coast. This dossier keeps the whole Cliopatria shape so that it stands alone if that choice is not made.

AFTER 1581. The row ends in 1581 only because Cliopatria then draws the same 99 cells in its Spanish Empire row (the Iberian Union row holds none of them). The Evolution page shows the holdings continuing under Portugal: Tangier to 1662, Mazagan to 1769, Elmina to 1637, Arguin to 1633, Cape Verde a crown colony from 1587, Mozambique a captaincy-general 1569-1609, Angola a crown colony from 1589. The Spanish Empire dossier (not this group's) should treat 1582-1640 as Habsburg rule over Portuguese colonies, or the colony dossiers should carry the cells.

CORRECTIONS ENTERED (all from pages): Socotra leaves in 1511, not 1534 (Evolution: possession 1506-1511); the Safi-Azemmour strip goes in 1541, not 1547 (conflicts page); Ksar es-Seghir and Arzila go in 1550 and Arzila returns 1577 (Evolution; the conflicts page has Alcacer Ceguer in 1549); Luanda is founded 1576, not 1579 (Portuguese Empire page); Arguin (1455-1633, one cell) is added.

NOT SETTLED. (1) Sao Tome, Fernando Po (Bioko) and the Zanzibar-Pemba-Mafia cells: no page opened dates them (the Portuguese Empire page has Fernao Gomes discovering Sao Tome and Principe after the 1469 grant, without a year; the Evolution page gives Sao Tome only as a crown colony from 1753). They stay as drawn, unverified. (2) The Inhambane and Zambezi-delta cells of 1534 and the Guinea cells of 1564: page silent (confidence 1). (3) Omitted from Cliopatria's shape though the Evolution page lists them: Agadir 1505-1541 and Mogador 1506-1510 (both in portuguese-morocco), Kilwa 1505-1512 (kilwa-sultanate has it as an occupation by 'portuguese-empire' to 1513), Malindi 'occupation (1500-1630)' (no land or counterpart named, not entered), Arguin (entered, in the found event and every correction). (4) Dates that disagree between pages: Arguin first feitoria 1445 (Portuguese Empire) or 1455 (Evolution); Mazagan 1506 (Evolution) or founded 1514-17 (conflicts); Alcacer-Ceguer abandoned 1549 or 1550; Tangier held to 1661 or 1662; Mozambique 'possession (1498-1501)' (Evolution) or territory established 1505 (Mozambique page). (5) The Portuguese Africa row has no African capital; Lisbon is entered. (6) Counterparts without dossiers: Socotra's rulers (not named on any page).

GAZETTEER NAMES NEEDED (real places the gazetteer lacks): Arguin (island, Mauritania, about 20.6 N 16.5 W), Asilah (Arzila), Ksar es-Seghir (Alcacer Ceguer), Socotra (island, Yemen, about 12.5 N 53.9 E). Radii used: Arguin 20 km, Asilah 15 km, Ksar es-Seghir 12 km (chosen so that, once added, they remove one Cliopatria cell each and spare the Ceuta cell at 35.80 N 5.42 W), Socotra 80 km (the whole island; 18 Cliopatria cells).
